title: The priestly blessing (Numbers 6:24–26)
hookLine: the Lord bless you and keep you, make his face shine on you
carry: the lord bless you and keep you

lines: TWO SILVER SCROLLS IN A TOMB.
cards: In burial caves just outside Jerusalem, archaeologists found two tiny rolled-up scrolls of silver, each small enough to hide in your palm, so fragile that unrolling them took great care.

Scratched into the silver were a few lines of Hebrew. Someone had worn them, perhaps as amulets, maybe around the neck. And the words inside were a blessing, the same one churches and synagogues still speak today.
Three lines people have been carrying close ever since.

teach.h: THREE LINES: THREE, FIVE, SEVEN WORDS.
teach.b: In the book of Numbers, God tells Moses to tell Aaron and his sons, the priests: this is how you shall bless the people.

Then the words, in the King James Bible: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace."
Three lines, and they grow. In Hebrew the first line is three words, the second five, the third seven, like a wave building. Each line names the LORD and gives two gifts.

Bless and keep: provide for you and guard you. Shine and be gracious: a face lighting up when it sees you, the way a grandparent's does when you walk in. Lift up his countenance: turn toward you, look right at you.
And the last word, the one everything builds to, is shalom: peace, wholeness, nothing missing. Notice it's thee, singular. The blessing is spoken to the whole people, but every you is a single you.
A crowd, blessed one person at a time. Then God says why: "they shall put my name upon the children of Israel; and I will bless them."

teach.h: THE LORD MAKE HIS FACE SHINE UPON THEE.
teach.b: God does the blessing. In synagogues it can be said by the kohanim, families who trace their line to the priests.
Churches use it too: some ministers and priests raise their hands and say it at the end of a service, at a wedding, over a newborn, at a grave.

how: Some pastors and priests say the Aaronic blessing at the end of worship with raised hands, and it is spoken at some weddings, baptisms and funerals; in synagogues, kohanim may say it over the congregation.

o: a quiet truce after a war has ended
a feeling of calm when you are alone
peace as wholeness, with nothing missing

games.q: you're a priest in Aaron's family, standing before the whole people. God has told you to bless them. what do you say?
o: the three lines God gave Moses for you.
games.why: the three lines given in Numbers 6, ending in peace. the priests speak them, and God says, I will bless them.

practice: Bring to mind one person, someone you love, someone you worry about, or someone you find hard, and see their face. Then say the old words over them slowly, one line per breath: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee.

The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee. The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace. If those words aren't yours, simply hold them in mind and wish them well.

wordCard.voice: Shalom. Hebrew for peace, wholeness, nothing missing: the last word of the priestly blessing, building like a wave from bless to peace.

orig.note: Hebrew: may he bless you, the first word of the blessing.

carryVoice: Your line: the lord bless you and keep you. People have carried those words close for a very long time. Until tomorrow.
